utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-04-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Please Your Honours, Joanna Korner and Ann Sutherland for the Prosecution assisted by Gina Butler, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: For the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Legal adviser in this case, lawyer Miljenko Dundjer because Ms. Sonja Turlakov, Defence counsel, is prevented from being here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. And we have the representatives of the government, I understand, if you would be kind enough to introduce yourself, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the government of the Republic of Yugoslavia, Savo Markovic, Minister of Justice in the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Markovic. And with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANCESKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Miodrag Panceski and I am the first secretary of the embassy of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. This is an application for provisional release made by this accused. We have seen the papers. We've read the guarantees. But if there are other matters which counsel wish to raise, now is the opportunity to do so. Mr. Dundjer it's for you to begin.

utterances.speaker: MS. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence remains with its motion for the provisional release of Mr. Momcilo Gruban and we would like to point out the following. In addition to the motion that we have submitted to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia, we have also submit add motion to the Republika Srpska, its bureau, a request to issues it's guarantees. A procedure is underway to obtain the guarantee from Republika Srpska. We are also in correspondence with the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the bureau of the Republika Srpska so that correspondence is under way. Both institutions in March, earlier this year, were informed about the wish and the desire of the accused Momcilo Gruban to voluntarily surrender himself to The Hague Tribunal. In that same period, the OTP and its representatives were informed about the desire of the accused Momcilo Gruban to voluntarily surrender to The Hague Tribunal. I would also like to say the following, if I may. If the Honourable Chamber so decides, I would like to inform the Honourable Chamber of the accused's future address in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This will be, if the Chamber will allow, the street of Aleksa Nenadovic number 1, apartment number 5, in Belgrade. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in fact, my learned friend has touched on a matter that I was going to raise before Your Honours. The fact of the matter is that this accused is, in fact, a native or comes from the area known as the Republika Srpska, Prijedor. That's where he resided up until the indictment was issued against him, now some seven years ago, and a public indictment, I should add. We had received or Your Honours have received the guarantee from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Serbia combined, but we were about to raise the matter that there is no guarantee from the Republika Srpska. Your Honours, the only things we would add to what we said in our reply is this: Surrender is perhaps not quite the word one would use in respect of this accused. He -- once the indictment was made public in February of 1995, it appears that the accused left the area of Republika Srpska and ended up, whether he's been there all along or not, we don't know, but in Serbia. The law on cooperation was passed between the federal republic and this Tribunal and at that stage, it would be our submission, it's not so much that Gruban surrendered himself but knew full well that he had no where else to go, and therefore in that event, rather than be arrested by the authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, actually gave himself up in order to make out the very application he's making before Your Honours today. Your Honours, all we say is this: It is entirely a matter for Your Honours, obviously. You've seen the guarantees, Your Honours are aware of the jurisprudence having very recently dealt with did in the case of Sainovic and I've forgotten the other gentleman's name now, Ojdanic, so I don't need to remind Your Honours of the authorities on it. There are of course in a very different position in that they are very senior members of the government. Your Honours we would suggest simply this: That the impetus for the accused to turn up for his trial is not particularly great. Omarska has been dealt with already in this Tribunal, and sentences ranging from five years at the lowest to 25 years at the highest have already been passed on those involved in that particular case. And Your Honours, all we would say is that there must be a pretty substantial risk that this man will not surrender himself for the trial in the light of what he knows to be the range of sentences that are possible. And we suggest that his failure to surrender himself, until such time as we suggest he had no where else to go, does not in fact reflect very highly in his favour or the likelihood of surrendering at a later stage. Your Honour, unless there are any other matters Your Honour would wish me to deal with, we have said everything we wish to in our written submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, thank you. Since the representative of the government has been good enough to come, the minister, it's right that he should have the opportunity to address us, if he would wish. Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge May. Your Honours, I have been authorised on behalf of the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the government of the Republic of Serbia to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. offer guarantees for the accused, Mr. Momcilo Gruban. The reasons that have inspired us to give this guarantee are contained in the text of the guarantee itself, but in view of the assertions made by Madam Prosecutor, I will have to read out certain things nevertheless so that they would be understood ad verbum and I would thereby confirm we are a serious state and that we are offering serious guarantees. By giving this guarantee, the federal government and the government of the Republic of Serbia are fulfilling their legal obligation based on Article 36 of the law on cooperation with The Hague Tribunal. Therefore, we make it incumbent upon ourselves to do the following: Number 1, the Yugoslav authorities make it incumbent upon themselves to take Momcilo Gruban from the Dutch authorities at Schipol airport at a date to be set by the Trial Chamber. Number 2, the Yugoslav authorities will provide escort to the accused to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Number 3 Yugoslav authorities make it incumbent possible themselves to escort the accused from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the mentioned airport and to hand him over to the Dutch authorities at a time, place and hour to be determined by the Trial Chamber. Number 4, the Federal Ministry of the Interior makes it incumbent upon itself, through the appropriate secretariat of the Republic of Serbia, to make sure that the accused reports daily to the police station, that a record is kept of this, and monthly written reports are forwarded to confirm that the accused is meeting these obligations and to inform the International Criminal Tribunal immediately of the possible absence of the accused. And last but not least, which is very important for what I'm saying now the Yugoslav authorities make it incumbent upon themselves to arrest the accused immediately if he tries to escape or violate any other condition of his provisional release and inform the International Criminal Tribunal, there of so that preparations can be made to hand him over to the Tribunal again. Your Honours, if we add to this the fact that the Defence counsel for the accused, Mr. Gruban, gave his address where he will reside, only a few minutes ago, and that this guarantee is supported by federal government and the government of the Republic of Serbia, that would all be very helpful to developing cooperation and trust between the International Criminal Tribunal and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and there would be very useful to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia the two republics of Yugoslavia, to support the dignity of the authorities of the country and the immediate authorities that cooperate with the Tribunal. Therefore we would find it indispensable to have these guarantees accepted. That is one point I wish to make. On the other hand, may I just give a few -- may I just say a few words in respect of the ruling made for Mr. Sainovic and Mr. Ojdanic, for their provisional release? Although it has not been confirmed yet, due to the appeal, this has been indeed welcome by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the people of the country have welcomed this and also they feel that hearings before this Tribunal are impartial. The people in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the people in both republics realised that indeed justice is being done here, not selective justice, and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia will thereby be in a position to contribute further to cooperation. Another thing that is so important by way of this ruling of the Trial Chamber, it gave a new impulse to cooperation between the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Hague Tribunal, and it seems to me now that this cooperation is becoming a two-way channel of communication, not only a one-way channel of communication as to now. I believe this been a meaningful venue. Other persons who have been indicted for serious crimes committed serious violations of humanitarian law in the territory of the former Yugoslavia would thereby be encouraged to surrender themselves to the Tribunal, and also the authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that are supposed to carry out the law and cooperate with The Hague Tribunal, would make it easier to carry out their job and I believe that things would become easier for the Tribunal as well. Your Honour Judge May, Your Honours, I am profoundly confident that the provisional release of Mr. Momcilo Gruban, along with the guarantees that I have just presented, would be a step in the right direction for both sides. There is no doubt in my mind that you will rule accordingly in this way I thank you once again and my very presence here today speaks of the attitude of the authorities of the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and also our belief in what you're doing. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, thank you for coming. As you'll appreciate we have to deal with every application on its own basis and on its own merits. And that we will do. Mr. Dundjer, since its your application, is there anything that you would like to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to add that this is a very honest man, who has a family, who has two children, who was never convicted before, who does not have any financial or any other personal reasons not to act in accordance with Rule 65 of the Rules of The Hague Tribunal, so I join the minister in what he has said. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell me where his family currently live?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently his family is in Maricka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm told that's in Prijedor, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before you rise, may I just, because it affects Gruban, we've had an application in respect of the old indictment from -- on behalf of Gruban, to set aside or deal with the jurisdiction of that indictment. I merely raise it at this stage. As Your Honours know, we filed last Friday, give or take, an application to amend all the indictments, including a joinder. I am merely asking Your Honours for guidance as to whether you would require a reply to an indictment, that in one way or another will be otiose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will rise now. We will consider this matter and give our judgement in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.18 p.m.
